```{r}
# 3 F solution
reduced = "short3"

```

```{r}
#get all items (pre-processed)
df.allitems <- read.csv(paste0(data_path, "/data/finalcollection/questionnaires/processeditemsUPDATED.csv"), header = TRUE)

# get overall scores 
df.allscores <- read.csv(paste0(data_path, "/data/finalcollection/questionnaires/processedsurvey.csv"), header = TRUE)

#get item manual 
itemmanual <- read.csv(paste0(data_path, "/data/finalcollection/questionnaires/itemmanual.csv"), header = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# select only those subjects that go on to be in analysis

df.allscores <- df.allscores[df.allscores$checks == 1,] #subset ppt that passed infrequency items
goodppt <- unique(df.allscores$PROLIFICID)
df.allitems <- df.allitems[df.allitems$PROLIFICID %in% goodppt, ]
```


```{r}
#missings mainly in CAPE, this is because of how it it set up on LS
df.allitems <- df.allitems[, !grepl("CAPE", names(df.allitems))]
df.allscores <- df.allscores[, !grepl("cape", names(df.allscores))]

#subset questionnaires 
#"IDAS", "IOU", "PSWQ"
df.allitems <- df.allitems[, !grepl("^TICS", names(df.allitems), ignore.case = TRUE)]
df.allscores <- df.allscores[, !grepl("^TICS", names(df.allscores), ignore.case = TRUE)]
df.allitems <- df.allitems[, !grepl("^STICSA", names(df.allitems), ignore.case = TRUE)]
df.allscores <- df.allscores[, !grepl("^STICSA", names(df.allscores), ignore.case = TRUE)] 
df.allitems <- df.allitems[, !grepl("^CTQ", names(df.allitems), ignore.case = TRUE)]
df.allscores <- df.allscores[, !grepl("^CTQ", names(df.allscores), ignore.case = TRUE)]

#which(colSums(is.na(df.allitems))>0)
length(df.allitems)
```


```{r}
#convert to numeric 
df.clean <- df.allitems
df.clean[,2:length(df.clean)] <- df.clean[,2:length(df.clean)] %>% mutate_if(is.character, as.numeric)

```


```{r}
#general
corr_type = "spearman"
nFactors = 3

trait_qs <- c("idas_score", "ius_score","pswq_score")
  strings_to_match <- c("PROLIFICID", "IDAS", "IOU", "PSWQ")
```



### Correlation of trait questionnaires
```{r}
df.scores <- df.allscores[colnames(df.allscores) %in% trait_qs]

cdf = cor(scale(df.scores), method = c(corr_type)) #z scoring here
colnames(cdf) <- trait_qs
rownames(cdf) <- trait_qs
cp <- corrplot(cdf, method='number')

```


### Correlation of single items
```{r}
df2 <- df.clean[, grep(paste(strings_to_match, collapse = "|"), names(df.clean))]
names(df2)

cdf <- cor(df2[,2:length(df2)], method = corr_type,use='complete.obs')
cp <- corrplot(cdf, tl.pos = 'n', method = "color") 
```

### Factor n solutions
```{r}
# a/ Eigenvalues
library(psych)
evals <- eigen(cdf)$values 
scree(cdf, factors = FALSE)
#plot(evals)
```

```{r}
# b/ Parallel analysis
# compares the scree of factors of the observed data with that of a random data matrix of the same size as the original.
set.seed(123) 
resPA <- fa.parallel(scale(df2[,2:length(df2)]), cor = "cor", fa = "fa", fm = "minres")

```

```{r}
# c/ Cattell-Nelson-Gorsuch indices
# CNG scree test

m <- nFactors::nCng(df2[,2:length(df2)], cor = TRUE, model = "factors", details = TRUE)
print(m) #nCng() finds the largest k such that the first k eigenvalues are “significantly” above random.
nf <- m$nFactors  

eig_df <- data.frame(
  Factor = seq_along(m$detail$values),
  Eigenvalue = m$detail$values
)

eig_df$highlight <- eig_df$Factor <= nf

eig_df$Factor <= nf 

ggplot(eig_df, aes(x = Factor, y = Eigenvalue, color = highlight)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_line(color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  labs(title = "Scree Plot of Eigenvalues",x = "Factor Number",y = "Eigenvalue") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)+theme(aspect.ratio = 1)+ scale_color_manual(values = c("#66D9FF","#ff00ff58"))


plotuScree(df2[,2:length(df2)], main=paste(m$nFactors," factors retained by the CNG procedure",sep=""))
```


```{r}
# d/ Multiple Regression Procedure
#computes the β indices, like their associated Student t and probability (Zoski and Jurs, 1993, 1996, p. 445). These three values can be used as three different indices for determining the number of components/factors to retain.
# https://rdrr.io/cran/nFactors/man/nMreg.html
m <- nMreg(df2[,2:length(df2)], cor = TRUE, model = "factors", details = TRUE)
print(m)
mdf <- data.frame(m$detail)
plotuScree(df2[,2:length(df2)], main=paste(m$nFactors[1], ", ",
                            m$nFactors[2], " or ",
                            m$nFactors[3],
                            " factors retained by the MREG procedures",
                            sep=""))
```

```{r}
# e/ Very simple structure
#Graphic output indicates the "optimal" number of factors for different levels of complexity
 
resvss <- vss(cdf, fm = "ml", n.obs = nrow(df), plot = TRUE) 
resvss
```


### Method agreement procedure 
```{r, results='asis'}
# https://www.r-bloggers.com/2018/05/how-many-factors-to-retain-in-factor-analysis/

res = parameters::n_factors(df2[,2:length(df2)], type="FA", rotation="oblimin")
#see::plots(res)
print(res)

print(xtable(data.frame(res)), type = "html")
dfrs <- data.frame(res)
dfrs
```

A)  3 factor solution
### Run factor analysis

```{r}
fa3 <- fa(cdf, nfactors = nFactors, rotate = "oblimin", fm = "ml", scores = "regression")
fa3.load <- data.frame(unclass(fa3$loadings))
fa3.load$varname <- rownames(fa3.load)
fa3.load <- merge(fa3.load, itemmanual, by="varname") #add items to get content
#fa3.load
```

```{r}
variance_table <- as.data.frame(t(fa3$Vaccounted))
variance_table
```




```{r  fig2, fig.width = 10, fig.asp = 0.8}
plot(fa3)

```


### Factor correlations
```{r fig3, fig.width = 10, fig.asp = 1}
cor.plot(fa3)
```


### Corrleation of loading
```{r}
cdf = cor(as.matrix(fa3.load[,grepl( "ML",colnames(fa3.load))]), method = c("pearson"))
cp <- corrplot(cdf,method = "number") 
```


```{r, fig5, fig.width = 10, fig.asp =0.5 }
#add column with main loading factor x item
fa3.load$manual_factor <- apply( abs(fa3.load[,colnames(fa3.load)[grepl("ML",colnames(fa3.load))]]),  1, which.max)
fa3.load$idx <- seq(nrow(fa3.load))

orig_factors = colnames(fa3.load)[grepl("ML",colnames(fa3.load))]

temp <- fa3.load[,c("idx","manual_factor","item")] %>%
pivot_wider(names_from = "manual_factor", values_from = "item")
temp <- temp[,!(colnames(temp) %in% c("idx"))]
temp <- temp[,paste(sort(as.integer(colnames(temp))))]
# !!! the below assumes ordering of columns by manual factor 1,2,3
temp <- plyr::ldply(apply(temp, 2, sort, decreasing=F),rbind)
#temp = t(column_to_rownames(temp))
temp = data.frame(t(temp))
temp <- temp[!(rownames(temp) %in% c(".id")), ]
colnames(temp) <- sprintf("F%s",seq(nFactors))
temp <- temp[,sprintf("F%s",seq(nFactors))]
colnames(temp) <- orig_factors

```

```{r}
#find max positive, not max absolute
fa3.load.long = fa3.load
fa3.load.long$loading = pmax(fa3.load.long$ML1, fa3.load.long$ML2, fa3.load.long$ML3)
fa3.load.long = fa3.load.long[,c("varname","item","manual_factor","scale", "measure","loading", "subscale","subscale_pure")]

#here
#manual 1 = MR3; manual 3 = MR2, manual 2 = MR1
```

```{r}
fa3.load.long = fa3.load
fa3.load.long$loading <- apply(
  fa3.load.long[, c("ML1", "ML2", "ML3")],
  1,
  function(x) x[which.max(abs(x))]
)
fa3.load.long = fa3.load.long[,c("varname","item","manual_factor","scale", "measure","loading", "subscale","subscale_pure")]

```


```{r}
df_long <- fa3.load %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("ML"),
    names_to = "ML_factor",
    values_to = "loading"
  )



custom_colors <- c(
  appetite_loss        = "#08519C",
  dysphoria            = "#66D9FF",
  well_being           = "#EDBC40",
  insomnia             = "#8BAEE8",
  lassitude            = "#0851E8",
  panic                = "#9D63BA",
  ill_temper           = "#90E0E8",
  suicidality          = "grey",
  traumatic_intrusions = "#EDBCBB",
  social_anxiety       = "#4C0048",
  appetite_gain        = "#C6E0FE",
  ordering             = "#0EB980",
  cleaning             = "#98B303",
  mania                = "orange",
  checking             = "#00B219",
  euphoria             = "#ED7840",
  traumatic_avoidance  = "#EDBCFF",
  claustrophobia       = "#E863E6",
  prospective_anxiety  = "#E8637F",
  inhibitory_anxiety   = "#91316D",
  worry                = "#CC33FF"
)
df_long <- df_long %>%
  arrange(subscale_pure, item) %>%      # order items by subscale
  mutate(item = factor(item, levels = unique(item)))


ggplot(df_long %>% mutate(ML_factor=factor(ML_factor, levels=c("ML2","ML1","ML3"), labels=c("Anxious-Depression","IoU-Worry","Well-being"))), aes(x=item, y=loading, fill=subscale_pure)) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + facet_wrap(~ML_factor, ncol=1, scales="free_x", strip.position="top") + scale_fill_manual(values=custom_colors, guide=guide_legend(nrow=1, title.position="top", label.position="bottom")) + theme_classic() + theme(axis.text.x=element_blank(), axis.ticks.x=element_blank(), strip.background=element_blank(), strip.text=element_text(size=12, face="bold"), panel.spacing=unit(1,"lines"), aspect.ratio=0.1, legend.position="bottom", legend.text=element_text(angle=90), legend.spacing.x=unit(0, "pt")) + labs(x=NULL, y="Loading", fill="Subscale") + geom_hline(yintercept=0)
```
